findings.problem: The empty state passes. `load_program` guards the work-items directory with `if os.path.isdir(items_dir)` and records nothing when it is absent. With PROGRAM.yaml present and program/work-items missing entirely, build_program_report returns parseErrors=[], total_count=0, aggregate=None, and STATUS.md renders 'none recorded' in every section with no indication the ledger source was absent. Worse, check_status_md (the `sbe program check` gate) then returns True on that state: I wrote STATUS.md from the empty ledger and check_status_md returned True. An absent source directory is NO-DATA, not a clean program, and this is the exact failure class the spec names ('another thing that can be silently absent and read as clean').
findings.fix: When os.path.isdir(items_dir) is false, append a parse error {path: 'program/work-items', reason: 'work-items directory is absent: NO-DATA, not an empty program'} and have render_status_md state it in the headline; make check_status_md return False whenever the report carries a NO-DATA source error. Add a calibrated test for the absent directory and for a present-but-empty directory.

findings.problem: `summary.excluded_count` is set to len(parse_errors), but parse_errors also collects unknown-depends_on entries appended at lines 828-832 for items that parsed fine and are fully included in every aggregate. Probe: one valid item naming two ghost dependencies yields items=1, excluded_count=2. The spec requires the summary to state how many items were excluded; this number is false in the founder-facing envelope.
findings.fix: Compute excluded_count from the load-time exclusions only (len(data.parse_errors) captured before the dependency errors are appended), or count distinct paths of errors whose item is not in `items`. Add a test asserting excluded_count==0 when the only parse error is an unknown dependency.

findings.problem: Nothing asserts the rendered risk table (spec STATUS.md section 7). I replaced the risk text in render_status_md with a hard-coded constant and all 32 tests still passed. The two risk tests assert only on the report dict, so the renderer could print an invented mitigation into STATUS.md and the suite stays green: the spec's required calibrated test 'a plain-string risk read without inventing a mitigation' is unproven at the layer the founder actually reads.
findings.fix: Add a test that calls render_status_md and asserts the table row contains the exact risk text and the literal 'no mitigation recorded' for a plain-string risk, and the recorded mitigation for a mapping risk. Calibrate it by breaking the renderer.

findings.problem: The gantt builds one section per item's own `wave` value, but the spec says 'One `section` per wave or milestone as recorded in PROGRAM.yaml'. On the real ledger PROGRAM.yaml records wave-0..wave-6 while the rendered sections are guided-experience, release-readiness, team-control. An item whose `wave` names no declared wave is accepted silently, unlike an unknown depends_on which is reported in parseErrors, so a mistyped or stale wave id is invisible.
findings.fix: Drive sections from program['waves'] (id/name as recorded), place items by matching wave id, render an explicit 'unassigned' section for items with no wave, and append a parseErrors entry naming any item whose wave is not a declared wave id.

findings.problem: _progress_for silently drops acceptance_met entries that are neither an in-range index nor an exact acceptance string. Probe: acceptance=['one','two'], acceptance_met=['bogus never listed', 99] yields progress_percent=0 with source 'derived from acceptance' and parseErrors=[]. Uninterpretable recorded data becomes a measured figure that counts toward measured_count and the aggregate, which is the same class of silent coercion the spec forbids by name for status values.
findings.fix: Raise ProgramParseError from _normalize_work_item naming the file and the offending acceptance_met entry when it is not an int in range or an exact member of acceptance, so the item is excluded rather than measured at a fabricated 0. Add a calibrated test.

findings.problem: In the risks table the risk text is pipe-escaped but the mitigation text is not. A recorded mitigation containing '|' emits a row with extra columns: probe produced '| A | r | not recorded | do a | b |', which markdown renders as a corrupted table.
findings.fix: Apply the same .replace('\n',' ').replace('|','\\|') normalization to mitigation_text (and to the severity/item cells) before formatting the row.

findings.problem: The gantt task line is 'title :tag, id, after..., duration'. Mermaid splits a gantt task on the first colon, so a work-item title containing a colon splits into the wrong name and metadata. Probe title 'Ship the thing, then verify: fast' renders 'Ship the thing, then verify: fast :active, A, 1d', which mermaid parses as name 'Ship the thing, then verify' plus garbage. No shipped title contains a colon today, so this is latent rather than currently broken.
findings.fix: Sanitize the task name before emission (replace ':' with a space or strip it) or fail the render naming the item id, and add a test with a colon-bearing title.

findings.problem: The state-file NO-DATA guard is defeatable by an empty file, and the PASS line then asserts a fact that was never measured. _budget_problem returns None whenever the state object has no 'budget' key, or when cap/spent are non-numeric. Verified via the real CLI: state file '{}' with a clean owed file -> exit 0 printing 'loop-open PASS: no unfinished, undeferred owed item and no exhausted budget were found.' Same PASS for {"budget":{"cap":"100","spent":100}} and {"budget":{"cap":null,"spent":999}}. A MISSING state file refuses as NO-DATA (exit 1), so writing an empty JSON object to the state path converts that refusal into an affirmative pass. This is the repository's known 'empty state passes' failure and it breaks SPEC.md line 10 ('Every claim a module prints must come from recorded state, never from a fresh judgement the module invented'): 'no exhausted budget were found' is a claim over an unmeasured budget. No test in the 55 covers an unmeasurable budget block.
findings.fix: Have _budget_problem distinguish 'not measurable' from 'clear' (return a NO-DATA sentence naming the absent or non-numeric cap/spent keys) and treat it the same way a missing state file is treated, OR, if a present-but-silent state file must not refuse, change the loop-open PASS text in main() to state the budget was not measured instead of asserting none was exhausted. Add a calibrated test for state={} and for cap/spent non-numeric.

findings.problem: The writer's openQuestion states a missing --state file is 'informational only (not blocking)'. It blocks. check_loop_open appends the missing-state sentence to `problems`, and main() refuses on any non-empty problems: verified `loop-open --state <absent> --owed <clean>` -> exit 1. The refusal text itself reads as informational ('so this run reports what it can from the owed-items file alone') while causing a refusal, and _budget_problem's docstring at line 226 justifies staying silent so as not to 'invent a third refusal reason the spec does not name' while the caller invents exactly that third refusal. Nothing in the 55 tests exercises a missing state file at all, in either direction.
findings.fix: Pick one behaviour and make text, exit code and docstrings agree. Either keep the refusal and reword the sentence to say plainly that loop-open is refused because budget spend cannot be confirmed, or return it on a separate informational channel that does not enter `problems`. Either way add a calibrated test asserting the exit code for a missing --state file.

findings.problem: The T3 tier_reason check is an `elif` after the agent_count branches, so an invalid agent_count masks it. Verified: brief {"tier":"T3","agent_count":"many"} with no tier_reason -> 'REFUSED (1 problem(s)): agent_count is 'many', not a positive integer'. tier_reason is never mentioned, so the agent fixes agent_count and comes back for a second round trip. SPEC.md line 236 requires output to name EVERY problem found, never only the first.
findings.fix: Split the T3 requirement out of the elif chain into its own `if dispatch_tier == "T3" and answered(brief.get("tier_reason")) is None:` so it is evaluated independently of the agent_count branch.

openQuestions: No shipped schema for program/OWED.json's loop-state companion file existed in the repo to mirror, so I designed one: {"schemaVersion":1,"budget":{"cap":N,"spent":M}}. If the orchestrator's real state writer uses different key names, loop-open's budget check will silently read as 'not measured' (no budget block found) rather than error, per the NO-DATA-on-absence-of-data design documented in _budget_problem's docstring -- it will not falsely block, but it also will not catch real overspend until the schema is reconciled.

A missing --state file (as opposed to a missing --owed file) is treated as informational only (not blocking), since the spec names only two refusal conditions (owed items, and a budget PROVEN exhausted by recorded numbers) and I did not want to invent a third refusal the spec never states; flagged here in case the orchestrator intended state-file absence to block symmetrically with owed-file absence.
